anchor.statement: Proposition 7.6. For every α ∈ R and every real two-vector Σ (R, Z, T) ∈ M α independent of the angular and auxiliary variables, (7.31) defines a linear operation L Σ . Its harmonic coefficients on the slow neighborhood satisfy the local derivative and envelope bounds of W α −1/2 , with smooth zero extension at the shell edges. With the slow cutoffs shown explicitly, its bounds and covariance are η β L Σ ∈ W α −1/2 , B(W 0 , L Σ ) = Σ , C( η β L Σ ) ∈ M 2 α −1 . (7.32) The denominator a σ remains this fixed coefficient at every correction stage. No sign or relative-size restriction is imposed on Σ in Proposition 7.6.

correspondence.by: Christian Garry (drafted with Claude Code; second review by ChatGPT, checked)
correspondence.note: phase_signedVector_class states that the √ε-scaled signed increment for target R ∈ M_{B−1/2−κ} lies in W_{B−κ}, with no sign condition on R and under determinant, entry and lower-weight bounds on the fixed primary matrix; cross_reconstruct and physical_signed_cross_covariance give the exact cross identity B(W0, LΣ) = Σ, signed_square_class a mean class for the square, and extendedIncrement_regular smooth zero extension at the shell edge. Getting (7.32) for Σ ∈ M_α requires choosing R = Σ/ε and tracking exponents (α−1 for R, α−1/2 for the wave, 2α−1 for the square) and checking that these declarations' hypotheses are met by the same coefficients; that bookkeeping is the reviewer's argument.
